title: Heart of the Matter 3
speaker: Nomon Tim Burnett
summary: The main teaching of this Soto Zen dharma talk is that by understanding and embracing the impermanence and interconnectedness of all things, we can break free from suffering caused by our own mental afflictions such as attachment, anger, and delusion. This involves letting go of a fixed sense of self and grasping for things that are ultimately empty of inherent existence. By doing so, we can find freedom and liberation in the present moment, rather than trying to escape or transcend it through meditation or other means.

So the Dalai Lama said:
*Destructive acts are motivated by disturbed states of mind.
That is to say, by a mind that is dominated by the afflictions.
In the entire history of human society it is these mental afflictions, these undisciplined states of mind, that underline humanity's destructive acts.
From the smallest act of killing a fly to the greatest atrocities of war, we must remember that ignorance itself is an affliction.
For example, when we fail to grasp the negative long-term consequences of an action and we instead act out of short-sighted thoughts of gain.
So ignorance itself is affliction.
For example, it is an example of ignorance when we fail to grasp the negative long-term consequences of an action and act out of short-sighted thoughts of gain.
If we closely examine the feeling of strong desire or strong anger, we will find that at the root of these emotions lies grasping at the object of the emotions.*
So let's pause a moment.

What does that feel like?

*And if we take it still further, we discover that at the root of all this lies grasping at our sense of self.
Not recognizing the emptiness of self and other, we mistakenly grasp at both as if they were autonomous, objectively real, and independently existent.
As the eighth-century philosopher Chandrakirti points out in his Guide to the Middle Way, we first grasp at the sense of self and then we extend this grasping onto others.
First you have a sense of I, then you grasp at things as mine.
By looking into our own minds, we can see that the stronger the grasping is, the more forcefully it generates negative and destructive emotions.
There is a very intimate causal connection between grasping at a sense of self and the arising of destructive emotions within us.
As long as we remain under the dominion of this erroneous belief, we'll have no room for lasting joy.
This is what it means to be imprisoned in the cycle of existence.
Suffering is nothing but existence enslaved to ignorance.*

And I think "destructive emotion" sounds a little dramatic, but he means all grasping, even the more subtle and quieter senses of being a little out of phase, or a little grouchy, or a little grumpy, or wanting things to be different from what they are.

*Although there are many afflictions and many ways of classifying them, three in particular, attachment, anger, and delusion, are always referred to as the three poisons of the mind.
Just as poison causes harm to the body and physical suffering, and can even bring one's life to an end, these mental afflictions also cause misery, perhaps even hastening our death.
Ultimately, mental afflictions not only cause suffering to ourselves and others, but they also obstruct our attainment of happiness.
In this sense, the internal states are our enemy.
These internal enemies are even more pernicious than any external enemy ever could be.
Even though we might at least stand a chance of hiding, we could hide from an external enemy, no matter where we go, mental afflictions can arise.
Furthermore, the internal enemy remains our enemy always.
There's not even the slightest chance that our internal enemy will become our friend at some point in the future.
There is no place in which we can escape this internal enemy, no way to win the enemy over to our side, and no way this enemy will cease its attack.*
So what can we do?
*We can understand emptiness.

At the moment of our first insight into the empty nature of self and reality, we start to break free, free of the enslavement of ignorance and the attack of the internal enemy.
By reducing our grasping, we start to undo the causal chain of unenlightened existence.
By undermining self-grasping ignorance, the first link of dependent origination, you prevent the arising of the second link and ultimately become free of the endless cycle of suffering lifetimes.*
